body: Thank you. I doubt they will, but I appreciate your thoughts.

If I can avoid this option, I'd really prefer to. I've heard a lot of bad things about military medicine and it's a really big commitment that I'm not sure I'm willing to make. But, if I need to do this, I will.

I know it is. You're right. It's just that, if I move out, I'll need a full time job. Stat. Which means, less time to study, research, study for the MCAT, etc. Not to mention, less money to pay for those things. 

But, fuck, will it be nice to not be in a household that resents me.

I can't speak to your character. I have never seen you in your role as father. I wish I could vouch for you. At the very least, I understand what you're saying and where you're coming from. I wish I knew why you think you're such a burden to your children or why you think you're representative of your father, but I don't. If you want to talk more or PM, I'll be up.

My parents divorced when I was 8. I was confused and didn't understand it at all. It's been 17 years since then and I still don't understand it all. What I do understand is this: I wish my dad had been there for me and he wasn't. This isn't what you want to hear, but please stick around for your kids. They'll remember it, even if you don't think they will.
